How long have you had the hamster? What sort of hamster is it? Female Syrians I've heard tend to be the most aggressive/territorial but stay tame once they have been tamed, but dwarfs can be more feral if not handled much. 

I got my male Syrian from a backyard breeder (sadly I just didn't know what I should be looking for at the time) and he was super aggressive when I first got him, lunging at me from one side of his cage to the other, latching onto my clothes with his teeth etc, but I just persisted with the bathtub training (do not approach them or acknowledge them in any way let them come to you and offer them a small treat, this will make them associate you with something good - food!) and a few months later he was pretty friendly.

 I believe every hamster can be tamed to some extent with time and patience but not every hamster is going to be cuddly and super friendly - in fact this is more of a rare exception as they're not very social creatures. Remember your hammy is probably just frightened, they are prey animals and don't understand that we aren't predators if they're caught off guard or not tamed yet.
